newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/WorldCom and MFS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/WorldCom and MFS.

text.p: Options on merger candidates WorldCom Inc and MFS Communications Co Inc highlighted trade on Monday as investors took advantage of sharp stock price movements.
The two companies early Monday announced a $14 billion merger agreement under which each common share of MFS would be exchanged for 2.1 common shares of WorldCom.
Shares of MFS rallied sharply while WorldCom fell on dilution fears, traders said.
By afternoon, MFS was up 9-7/8 at 44-3/4 and WorldCom fell 3-3/4 to 22-5/8.
The two stocks were by far the most actively traded on the Nasdaq market.
WorldCom options drew most activity as some investors played the stock's decline and others positioned themselves for a recovery in the stock.
"There's been a lot of call buyers and sellers," said the WorldCom specialist at the Pacific Stock Exchange.

"There still is some possibility that this deal won't go through and that the stock might bounce back to where it came from," he said. "I think that might be some of the speculation with the call buying."
Most of the activity in WorldCom calls was seen in the September series but the most active call was the December 25, which traded 2,230 contracts. The option fell two to 1-5/8.
In the September series, the WorldCom September 25 call traded 1,450 contracts, the 22-1/2 traded 1,150 and the 20 and 30 each traded about 1,025 contracts.
The specialist said retail investors were buying and selling the calls while broker/dealers and the floor crowd had been largely call sellers.
He added that the public had been actively selling the most active WorldCom 22-1/2 put in early trading.
The September 22-1/2 put, which traded nearly 600 contracts, was up 11/16 at 15/16.
"I don't think there was any speculation" about the deal, the specialist said. The options activity "seems pretty routine for a $4 move in a pretty heavily traded stock."
Trading in MFS options was notably slower than in WorldCom, with calls attracting most interest. Most of the options activity was seen on the CBOE.
MFS options trade on the CBOE, the Pacific Stock Exchange and the American Stock Exchange.
The most active MFS September 40 call traded a combined 1,131 contracts, most of which crossed on the CBOE, where it rose 4-11/16 to 5-1/8.
The 40 strike calls were active in the November series while the 45s drew interest in the February 1997 series.
Another merger-related stock that saw relatively heavy options trading was Conseco Inc, traders said.
The insurance company on Monday announced a four-pronged aquisition plan valued at $2.04 billion.
The stock rallied 2-1/2 to 44-1/2. --G. Crawford, (312) 408-8750/E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
